120	Afterwards, if you waited with him, and he was a flower of a young man, and you waited until he would marry, and in the end
121	you said, why not, let him persevere a little more, what, a millstone around his neck and he studies Torah?
122	In the end he saw something, someone took him somewhere, and then the bitterness worked on him: "a root bearing gall
123	and wormwood."
124	That is what came out.
125	Therefore, truly, the most correct approach is to marry as early as possible.
126	Not in a panic, not in haste, not in a rush, but with careful thought, with Torah guidance,
127	with understanding, but this is the right direction.
128	That is how it is proper to act, not to delay too much.
129	But Yitzchak was 40, the fathers of the world, they were different.
130	So why did he marry only at 40?
131	He could have married earlier, what happened?
132	What happened?
133	In the Akeidah, Rashi writes on Bereshit 22:20.
134	Rashi writes: "On his return from Mount Moriah, the Holy One, blessed be He, informed him
135	that his soulmate Rivkah had been born."
136	So what do you want, that he should have started earlier?
137	Until now they had not told him.
138	So what, he was 37, what, now you waited?
139	I waited for prophecy from the Creator, blessed be He, to tell me. My father wanted to examine the vineyard of Israel by good traits,
140	by values, by love of Torah, love of others, by purity.
141	My father wanted...
142	He went, traveled far distances to bring me a good wife, so in any case
143	Avraham waited and Yitzchak waited to receive word, when they knew
144	that it was already the time, she was three years old, her arrival came.
145	How old was he when he married?
146	Forty.
147	If she was born at the Akeidah, how old was she when she came to marry
148	him?
149	Three.
150	A little girl. From a very simple calculation, never mind that the Midrash says some say fifteen, some say fourteen,
151	there are discussions about this, but three years old, it is hard for us to picture today. Not a girl of three who loves camels,
152	a three-year-old girl goes and brings, and says, "I will go."
153	As if, Rashi writes, "I too am not asking you, I will go."
154	What does it mean, not asking them?
155	Apparently it is interpreted with a negative connotation, what, I am not asking them?
156	Your parents tell you, sit quietly.
157	That is why her parents were afraid, and sent her mother along with her.
158	And this Devorah...
159	What was her nurse called?
160	Devorah, Rivkah's nurse.
161	"And Devorah died there, under the oak."
162	Who is this Devorah?
163	Rivkah's nurse.
164	Who is a nurse?
165	Her mother, the wife of Betuel.
166	That is what Rashi writes, her nurse.
167	She went with her and said, my daughter I am not sending alone, a three-year-old girl, are you crazy?
168	You with your money, with your greed, you are like your father, you...
169	What do you want?
170	Why me?
171	Listen, I'm telling you, that one died, you are next.
172	You are not, no, no, sending my girl, three years old, what, are you crazy?
173	So they came to me, and you say, her mother and her brother, "let her stay with us a year or ten, then she will go," "do not
174	delay me, since HaShem has made my journey successful."
175	"Let us call the girl and ask her opinion." From here the Gemara learned that we do not marry off a girl without asking her. "Will you go?" "I will go!"
176	So if the question was clear enough, I cannot do anything about it.
177	She wants it, she saw the young man, understood that this is her match, afterwards, what will happen?
178	If she does not marry, she will blame me all her life, why didn't she marry?
179	You know how many stories I have, of stories where parents interfered in a crude way, not where they
180	should have interfered, because there are places where they must interfere.
181	And not where they should have interfered, and in the end they stayed single, and blamed
182	their parents all their lives, that because of them they were not allowed to marry whom they wanted, in the end that is what came
183	of it.
184	Why do you need this?
185	You know, I have a shocking story, I don't want to give too many details, so that not...
186	Many times I give details and stories, and afterwards they ask me why did you say it, yes you said...
187	Tell it.
188	Tell it?
189	So once Moshe told me that...
190	You said, tell it.
191	I once gave a talk at a center in Holon, a big Holon.
192	And I was there...
193	And I arrived there, and someone came to me, said to me, Rabbi, give me a blessing, I have three children,
194	over the age of 40, who did not marry.
195	I said to him, how is this thing?
196	It is painful for parents, there is nothing like it.
197	"May you see children of your children, peace upon Israel," there is nachas.
198	Three sons not married, he says to me, Rabbi, do you know what the biggest paradox is?
199	I said to him, what?
200	That my wife is a matchmaker.
201	I said to him, now you have solved the mystery for me, why are they not married?
202	He says to me, why?
203	I said to him, go ask your wife whether many times she acted as if she were the Holy One, blessed be He.
204	She decided, this one doesn't suit her, he doesn't suit him, that one doesn't suit her.
205	What was it?
206	He went and checked, afterwards looked for me, came to me.
207	He says to me, Rabbi, you are a prophet.
208	I said to him, neither a prophet nor the son of a prophet.
209	All the measures of the Holy One, blessed be He, Sotah page 9, are measure for measure.
210	She broke up matches because she went out with so-and-so, now she is the matchmaker, yes?
211	So she says to her, I want.
212	And what was there?
213	The girl wanted, the young man wanted, and her friend suddenly called, that her daughter
214	was in the matchmaking process, so she called the girl and said, the young man is not interested, and took that young man
215	and matched him with her friend's son.
216	And not once and not twice, because she was strong and domineering, and she would do wrongs, and think
217	there is no judgment and no Judge, and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought it to her, into her own house,
218	there is no fear of Heaven.
219	There is money, you have one, but if it were not his match, he would say no, and they would find
220	each other. Clear your conscience with stories, wait, and this is what you received in this world, what will you receive
221	in the World to Come?
222	How much Torah guidance is needed. If the matchmaker is not connected to Torah guidance, one must be careful of him, keep away
223	from him.
224	What are you, for money?
225	They said "shadchan" stands for: liars, speaking, taking money.
226	Only for the money, tell you stories?
227	For some greed of his.
228	So even if he does it for the sake of Heaven, he needs Torah guidance.
229	Why, what, only because of the money?
230	On the contrary, it is worthwhile to pay, because he is responsible, because he will call, because he will search.
231	But when they do it for free, many times, as the Zohar says, Terumah 128b, anything done for free is from the Sitra Achra.
232	
233	Redeem it, pay something, give him a tip.
234	Even if he did not ask for money, buy a gift, give.
235	Never leave tails behind you.
236	Whoever did something for you...
237	Take out, buy, bring, improve, smooth things over.
238	Never be like the Sitra Achra that only draws, takes.
239	Be like the Sitra of holiness, give: "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing."
